svg.aria-label: Animation: the same checkout with a transactional outbox and with pg_txn. Outbox: the API service writes the order and an outbox row, a relay polls it, publishes to a broker and marks it sent, a worker consumes it, checks Redis for duplicates, charges the payment API and writes the result back with a version check, and on failure a retry / DLQ topic and a DLQ handler take over: 10 network hops across 5 services plus Redis. pg_txn, a SQL schema plus a library in the app on stock PostgreSQL: run 1 reads and owns the order in a short DB transaction, reaches the charge and rolls back, so no transaction, lock or connection is held while the app charges the payment API with the effect id as idempotency key; the result is recorded in PostgreSQL; run 2 writes paid, spawns the receipt and commits atomically in one DB transaction; after the commit the app's in-process worker sends the receipt. On failure the app retries the charge with the same key and the retry is recorded in PostgreSQL: 6 hops, 1 service, one function.
svg.title: Transactional outbox vs pg_txn
svg.text: pg_txn: the transactional outbox, local to your transaction, plus effects in the middle of it that hold no locks or connections

g.text: an API service, a relay, a broker, a worker, a DLQ handler and Redis
the API writes the order and an outbox row in one transaction
the relay polls the outbox table (or CDC tails the WAL)
the relay publishes OrderPlaced to the broker (Kafka, SQS)
the relay marks the outbox row sent
the worker service consumes the message
the worker asks Redis: already processed?
the worker charges, with an idempotency key it manages
the worker writes 'paid' back, guarded by a version check
if the charge fails instead: timeout
the worker nacks: the message goes to the retry / DLQ topic
a DLQ handler consumes it: re-publish later, or page someone
+ an outbox table, topics, a DLQ and Redis keys to keep in step
+ a relay, a broker and a worker service to deploy, scale and watch
10 hops · 5 services + Redis · your code in 4 places
the charge hasn't run yet: ROLLBACK.
nothing is held while it runs
the app charges, keyed by the effect id
the result is recorded in Postgres
after the commit, the app's own
done: one function, nothing else runs
if the charge fails instead: timeout
the failure is recorded in Postgres,
the app retries with the same key:
your code for this checkout: checkout.ts
